claims.claim_text: Indexed First Lieutenant Anthony Scariano is strongly identified as the Chicago lawyer and judge who served with OSS in northern Italy.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official Illinois memorial resolutions and a first-person institutional oral history document his OSS service and distinctive life chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact distinctive name, indexed officer grade and multiple independent institutional sources explicitly naming OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place college before wartime OSS service and legal education after the war.
claims.match_notes: The Senate resolution's sequencing language is inconsistent, so the project does not infer an exact recruitment date.

sources.locator_override: OSS intelligence-officer service in northern Italy
First-person account of OSS service in Italy in 1945

claims.claim_text: Anthony Scariano was a student at George Washington University and graduated in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An Illinois Senate memorial resolution identifies the university and 1942 graduation year.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on exact distinctive name and corroborated OSS biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before the 1945 OSS service described in Scariano's oral history, but not proven to be immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: Student status is not employment and is excluded from employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Sergeant Chester A. Scerra is strongly identified as the Army veteran whose obituary records an OSS assignment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army crosswalk agrees in exact name and private identifier; the exact-name obituary independently states OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from two independent sources and a unique protected-identifier match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The obituary documents wartime service but supplies only postwar employment, which is not used here.
claims.match_notes: Private identifiers and postwar details are excluded from the public claim.
